examples.summary: A terminal trading desk for one market: HMAC signing by hand, the op-envelope WebSocket protocol, exact decimal money, and a write path that places one order and guarantees it is cancelled.
A bulk order loader: a file of orders in, POST /orders/batch in weight-optimal chunks out, paced against the rate-limit budgets it reads from the venue. Dry-runs by default.
A local L2 book replica for one market over the public WebSocket: ordered by sequence, re-snapshotted over REST on every gap or reconnect, and cross-checked against the REST book.
Watches one account against exposure, loss and margin limits, and cancels resting orders when one is breached (with --arm).
How far each mark can move before maintenance margin breaks, ranked by fragility, next to the venue's own ADL record.
Place-to-ack, place-to-WS, cancel-to-ack and cancel-to-WS latency percentiles from post-only orders that cannot fill. Dry-runs without --live.
Watches one account against exposure, loss and margin limits, and cancels resting orders when one is breached (with --arm).
Arms cancel-on-disconnect, then kills its own trading session so you can watch the venue cancel for you. Dry-runs by default.
An entry plus native take-profit and stop-loss exits sized to the fill, kept one-cancels-other over the WebSocket and reconciled over REST. Dry-runs without --live.
Works one parent order as timed IOC children under a price guard, and survives being killed mid-slice by reconciling against the venue. Dry-runs without --live.
Watches one account against exposure, loss and margin limits, and cancels resting orders when one is breached (with --arm).
Delegates trading to a scoped, expiring agent key and revokes it again, reading the EIP-712 signing domain from the venue. --dry-run needs no credentials.
Runs CCXT-shaped code against Nexus through the adapter, side by side with the native client, measuring what the unified layer costs. Market data only.
Reviews one account over the MCP tool surface, with an explicit read-only allowlist. Exit code 2 on a breach, so it works from cron.
A ladder of resting post-only orders on one market, kept by a crontab-able reconciler over the CLI, idempotent through derived client order ids. Dry-runs without --commit.
Why you cannot reach the venue, one check at a time: DNS, path prefix, WebSocket base, clock skew, then credentials. Read-only; output is safe to paste into a bug report.
Follows your account's channels over the WebSocket and survives a disconnect: a durable per-channel cursor, a resume checked for holes, and the out_of_sync path.
A venue-wide market report (candles, funding, volume, event stats) as a terminal table, a CSV and a self-contained HTML page. No credentials, no dependencies.
A period P&L, fee and funding statement for one account, reconciled against the venue's own equity curve with the residual reported. Lossless decimal money.
Ranks markets by funding carry and how stable it has been, against the margin it ties up. Derives the settlement interval instead of assuming 8h.
